concerns.text: T002 is too coarse for one task: it bundles (a) neutral-prompt curation, (b) conflicting-variant generation, (c) curated_prompts.csv construction, (d) the entire human-annotation protocol + aggregation + merge, and (e) unit tests. Split so the atomizer/executor can verify each deliverable independently (e.g., generation vs. annotation collection vs. merge).

T008 runs hypothesis tests (a)–(d) (primary, neutral, filler control, empty control) but the contract schema's `tests` object and `multiple_comparison_correction.adjusted_p_values` only define `primary` and `robustness` keys. The neutral/control test results have no representable home in the contract-conformant report.json, so the task's own check ('conforming to the schema') cannot be satisfied while reporting all tests. Schema or task must specify where these land (e.g., an additional `secondary_tests` block).

T004 leaves the verifier model ambiguous: 'e.g., `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct` or the published Edit-R1 distilled checkpoint on HF'. An implementer cannot deterministically execute this; name ONE exact HF model ID (and record it in quickstart provenance) so baseline and augmented conditions provably use the same model.

T009 never specifies the hold-out set size. SC-005's effect-size-difference test (p ≥ 0.05) is not executable/verifiable without an N for the hold-out conflicting set and the number of human raters per hold-out prompt; state both (e.g., 'N conflicting hold-out prompts, ≥3 raters each').

T002's check requires `n_raters ≥ 3` in human_validation.csv, but the data model §6 defines only `prompt_id, human_rating, annotation_source`. The check is unverifiable against the declared contract — either update the data model to include `n_raters` or restate the check against the existing columns.

SC-007 (Pearson r ≥ 0.5) and SC-008 (Cohen's d ≥ 0.5) are threshold criteria, but T008 only computes/reports them and T010's validation_checks.json list does not include pass/fail assertions for these two thresholds. Add an explicit assertion step so the criteria are evaluated, not merely reported.

T013's check 'reproduces the result artifacts within deterministic tolerance' does not name the tolerance or which artifacts/fields it applies to (figures byte-stable? CSV values to what precision?). Specify, e.g., 'CSV numeric columns match to 1e-9; figures byte-identical'.
